lessons: Tonight WG went 3-0 on a low curve of Avacyn's Pilgrim, Doomed Traveler and two Gatstaf Shepherd, with Bonds of Faith and Rally the Peasants closing 13 to 33 turn games, which supports the guide's cheap-curve-plus-closers advice.

Tonight contradicted the guide's 'do not take Galvanic Juggernaut' line only partly: my colourless top-end was a fine third-colour-free finisher, but I'd still take Bonds of Faith or a flier over it, and the guide's 'avoid 3-colour bloat' stands.
My 15 cheap ground creatures stalled against WG's Somberwald Spider and Villagers of Estwald, and games ran 17 to 33 turns, so prioritise fliers or evasion over more 2-drops.
Sensory Deprivation, my pack 3 first pick, is black removal I left out of the BR deck, yet WG's blockers were what beat me, so play cheap removal even at a small cost to the curve.
Devil's Play, my pack 1 first pick, went unplayed in GW; commit to a lane by mid pack 1 and stop taking off-colour bombs, since Spider Spawning also sat idle.
The guide says fliers win, yet my flier-less GW needed 22 and 32 turns to beat WB, and BR games ran 14 to 19 turns; prioritise evasive creatures over ground filler.
Two Rebuke and two Blazing Torch looked too few answers; I lost round one 1-2 to BR, so take a third cheap removal spell over Festerhide Boar, which the guide already calls filler.
Black-red's removal core of Victim of Night, Tribute to Hunger, and Brimstone Volley, backed by a Vampire and Zombie curve, won both matches it closed out, so take cheap removal early.
I lost 0-2 to seat 0's green-white deck, the table's 3-0 leader with Bonds of Faith and Mentor of the Meek, so draft more answers to its combat tricks.
Late-pack duplicates of Rage Thrower and Markov Patrician were filler; spend those picks on higher-impact black or red playables instead.
Four fliers and four removal in my WB still went 1-2, losing 0-2 to UG and WG in 24 and 32 turn grinds, so take card-advantage finishers over Walking Corpse filler.
Where tonight contradicted the guide: my 11 Plains/6 Swamp white-first WB with Dead Weight, Corpse Lunge and Smite went 1-2, while the guide's matching build went 3-0, so the split is no guarantee.
Cheap Cathars and Avacynian Priest curved out to a 2-0 over UR, but the 24 and 32 turn losses showed a cheap curve must close; take fliers that win grinds over a fourth ground body.
Don't spend late picks on a second Delver of Secrets or Frightful Delusion; I cut both, so those picks were wasted. Take playable two- and three-drop creatures, since UR still needed 23 spells.
Round 1 and 2 losses came in 15-23 turn games against WB and WU, and my UR deck had little card advantage. Prioritize Think Twice-style draw or flyers over Traitorous Blood and Vampiric Fury.
Claustrophobia, Harvest Pyre, and the two Scourge of Geier Reach anchored the 2-0 win over BR in 21- and 30-turn games. Prioritize that removal and Scourge package early.
Don't play Spider Spawning without self-mill enablers: my UG deck ran it with none, though the guide says it only works in that build, so cut it or draft Armored Skaab-style enablers.
Tonight's round 3 loss (1-2 to WG, whose list included Somberwald Spider) argues against blind 'fliers win': draft reach or flier answers beyond Prey Upon.
Take the green-blue flier lane early: Murder of Crows, Moon Heron and Lantern Spirit were available, and my rounds 1-2 went 4-0 in games.
Drafting without a guide, my WU tempo deck went 2-5 in games; its Round 1 loss to UG ran 30 turns, so prioritise a late-game threat or two over extra cantrips like Think Twice.
Keep a cheap ground defender: cutting One-Eyed Scarecrow left me thin against UG's Festerhide Boar and Villagers of Estwald, and BR's Round 3 curve beat me in a 14-turn game.
